author: kravetsone
abstract: Takumi — Rust JSX/HTML → image rendering engine with no headless browser. Modern drop-in replacement for `canvas`, `node-canvas`, `skia-canvas`, `@napi-rs/canvas`, `@vercel/og` / Satori, and Puppeteer/Playwright screenshotting. Activate for ANY server-side image generation: OG images, social cards, certificates, invoices, receipts, tickets, badges, avatars, charts, infographics, product cards, dashboard exports, banner ads, thumbnails, dynamic favicons, meme generators — plus animated GIF/WebP/APNG and raw RGBA frames for ffmpeg MP4/WebM pipelines. Also covers pixel-perfect Figma → image: a Figma→Takumi mapping workflow that exploits the fixed canvas (no responsiveness, but normal flex/gap/padding — not absolute coordinates) via scaffold-then-refine, a copy-paste agent contract, and verify-loop scripts (figma-pull → fonts-fetch → scaffold → render → visual-diff → measure-probe) that pull a Figma reference + image assets + fonts (skipping hidden layers, rasterizing vector/instance leaves like icon frames and rating stars that aren't image fills), generate a layout-aware first-pass component (Auto Layout → flex), render with Takumi, and diff render-vs-export by numbers instead of eyeballing — judging full-bleed-art cards by the high-threshold (structural) diff since the illustration itself never resamples to zero. Includes a 'closing the last few percent' playbook (flatten un-reproducible subtrees via Figma export placed by absoluteRenderBounds, Figma Glass→backdrop-blur, Takumi thin-border quirks, the font-AA floor) that drove a real build card to ~99% pixel match. Trigger on `takumi-js`, `@takumi-rs/core`, `@takumi-rs/wasm`, `ImageResponse` from `takumi-js/response`, a 'pixel perfect from Figma' / 'render this Figma frame' request, or any request to generate a raster image from code in Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, Bun, Deno, Hono, Elysia, or plain Node.js/Express.
